sentences.text: Mandschurosaurus is an extinct genus of hadrosaurid dinosaurs, meaning 'duck-billed lizard,' named 'lizard from Manchuria' based on fossils from China and possibly Laos.
The largest known specimen measured 11.24 meters long, 6.48 meters tall, and weighed between 1.5 and 2 metric tons.
This genus holds the distinction of being the first dinosaur genus ever named from China.
A mounted skeleton of the holotype is displayed at the Central Geological and Prospecting Museum in St. Petersburg, though much of it is made of plaster.
The holotype of Mandschurosaurus amurensis is a poorly preserved skeleton collected by Russian scientists in 1914 from the banks of the Amur River in China.
The holotype was originally described as Trachodon amurense by Riabinin in 1925 before being reassigned to the new genus Mandschurosaurus in 1930.
Fossils of Mandschurosaurus were found on the right bank of the Amur River near Blagovéshchensk, Russia.
The first species collected, Mandschurosaurus amurensis, was found in 1914 and formally described in 1930 by Riabinin.
Mandschurosaurus belongs to the subfamily Hadrosaurinae, the family Hadrosauridae, and the class Ornithischia.
Several species have historically been assigned to the genus Mandschurosaurus, including M. mongoliensis, M. jiainensis, and M. laosensis.
Mandschurosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago, in the Campanian stage of Asia.
The time range for Mandschurosaurus spans from the Aptian to the Maastrichtian, between 121.4 and 66 million years ago.
The validity of the genus Mandschurosaurus is debated, with some researchers considering it a nomen dubium while others regard it as a valid taxon.
Research suggests that M. mongoliensis is a synonym of Gilmoreosaurus and M. laosensis may be a nomen dubium that was not actually a hadrosaurid.
